issues.legal_issue: A person who occupies premises only as a relative of a gratuitous licensee, without an independent legal right to occupy them, is not entitled to an interim injunction protecting that occupation.
material_facts: The deceased owner’s interest in the property had been bequeathed to other co-owners, and the will created no interest in the property for the occupant or the occupant’s maternal grandmother.
The grandmother was allowed to occupy the premises without payment, out of affection and sympathy, and was therefore a gratuitous licensee.
The occupant was staying with the grandmother and claimed no independent right to the premises.
The occupant sought an interim injunction against dispossession without due process; the trial court refused it, and the High Court reversed that refusal.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court’s order, and restored the trial court’s refusal of interim injunction. It clarified that its observations did not decide the merits of the pending suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rame Gowda (Dead) by LRs. v. M. Varadappa Naidu (Dead) by LRs. and Others, (2004) 1 SCC 769, settled possession must be effective, undisturbed, and known to the owner or not concealed; occupation as an agent or servant at the owner’s instance is not actual physical possession. Under Maria Margarida Sequeira Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeira, (2012) 5 SCC 370, a person allowed to stay gratuitously acquires no right or interest through long occupation, and court protection of occupation is available to a person with a valid subsisting rent, lease, or licence agreement. No statutory provision was relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_interlocutory_injunction_order and occupant_is_relative_of_gratuitous_licensee and occupant_claims_no_independent_right and not occupant_has_valid_occupancy_agreement

predicates.appeal_from_interlocutory_injunction_ord: The case is an appeal concerning an order on an application for interim protection against dispossession.
predicates.occupant_is_relative_of_gratuitous_licen: The occupant stayed in the premises as a relative of a person who had been permitted to occupy them gratuitously.
predicates.occupant_claims_no_independent_right: The occupant did not claim a right to occupy the premises independent of the person with whom they were staying.
predicates.occupant_has_valid_occupancy_agreement: The occupant had a valid, subsisting agreement granting a right to occupy the premises.
predicates.interim_injunction_protection_denied_to_: Interim injunctive protection of the gratuitous occupant’s possession is refused.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns interim protection against dispossession and the occupant is staying as a relative of a gratuitous licensee, claims no independent right, and has no valid occupancy agreement, the occupant is denied interim injunctive protection.
